r: Sun-synchronous, near-polar; passes a place at the **same local solar time** – PSLV's speciality

Extra motors fixed to the core for lift-off thrust

5.x: **Eastward launch:** uses the Earth's **west-to-east rotation** (a free speed boost); sites **nearer the equator** gain most. The boost does not give escape velocity – an orbiting satellite never reaches **escape velocity**.
**Polar / SSO launches** go **southward** (from Sriharikota a **dog-leg around Sri Lanka**).
**Sriharikota** (**SDSC-SHAR**, Andhra Pradesh), on the **east coast**: rockets fly over the sea; all Indian orbital launches, including private ones, go from here.

6.x: **Early GSLVs** flew **Russian KVD-1** cryogenic stages; technology transfer was refused in the **1990s**, so India built its own. **First indigenous cryogenic success: GSLV-D5 (Jan 2014)**; GSLV-D1 (**2001**) used the Russian stage.
**C25 (2017):** the **C25** cryogenic upper stage with the **CE-20** – India's first high-thrust indigenous cryogenic engine – was ground-tested for **GSLV Mk III**.
